findings.title: deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: Throwing `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` from a tRPC handler surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) rather than a 403/404, and the message may be scrubbed in production. Use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` so the client can distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault.

findings.title: Credential ownership check misses team/delegation credentials
findings.body: The handler only matches `credential.userId === user.id`. Credentials attached to a team (userId null, teamId set) or delegation-derived credentials will never match, so deleting their cache always fails; conversely there is no check that the user is allowed to act on team credentials at all. Consider mirroring the authorization logic used by `viewer.credentials.delete` (user OR team admin/owner) so behaviour is consistent and complete.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired caches are reported as fresh
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all CalendarCache rows for the credential with no `expiresAt` filter. The UI then shows "Cache Status / Last updated: …" for credentials whose cache entries are already expired and will no longer be served, which misleads users into believing caching is active. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry explicitly).

findings.title: deleteCache success does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, but the deleteCache mutation only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. In the Alert branch of SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper (and anywhere `onChanged` is not passed) nothing invalidates the query, so the dropdown keeps showing a stale "Last updated" timestamp for a cache that was just deleted. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the mutation's onSettled.

findings.title: Timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` formats the cache timestamp with US month/day ordering and 12-hour clock regardless of the user's locale/time format preference, producing confusing dates for non-US users. Use the user's locale (e.g. from `useLocale()`) or the existing date formatting helpers.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data relies on implicit @updatedAt and adds a write per cache refresh
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is intended to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but it passes an empty data object, so it only has an effect if the model declares `@updatedAt`; otherwise it is a silent no-op while still issuing an UPDATE over every selected calendar of the credential on each cache population. The PR notes also state this value is never consumed by the frontend. Either set the field explicitly (`updatedAt: new Date()`) and document the consumer, or drop the call.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and ENV_FILE path is cwd-dependent
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` fails on GNU sed (Linux), where `-i ''` is interpreted as an empty script file name, so the script cannot update .env on Linux/CI. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so running the script from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` outside the repository.

findings.title: Migration header comment contradicts the statement
findings.body: The generated warning says the column was added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", yet the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning in place is confusing for anyone auditing migrations; remove or correct it.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency
findings.body: `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` relies on npx fetching `tsx` from the network at run time (and may prompt for install), while `ts-node` remains a devDependency. Add `tsx` to devDependencies and invoke it via the local binary for reproducible, offline-capable runs.

findings.title: No tests for new cache-status enrichment or deleteCache handler
findings.body: The new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` repository method, the enrichment in connectedCalendarsHandler, and the deleteCache handler (including its authorization branch) have no unit tests. Given the authorization check in deleteCache guards data deletion, at least a test covering a credential owned by another user should be added.
